title: Mixed Bed Polisher

introduction.definition: A mixed-bed polisher contains cation and anion resins mixed intimately in one vessel. The water meets H⁺ and OH⁻ sites alternately thousands of times, like many two-bed units in series, giving very pure water. To regenerate, the resins are separated by backwashing, regenerated separately with acid and caustic, and re-mixed with air.
applications: Polishing after RO or two-bed DM for high-pressure boilers
introduction.summary: A mixed-bed polisher contains cation and anion resins mixed together, producing very high-purity water. For regeneration the resins are separated by backwashing, regenerated separately and re-mixed with air.

pressure.title: Thousands of tiny demineralisers in series
pressure.description: In service the cation and anion beads are mixed, so the water meets alternate H⁺ and OH⁻ exchange sites thousands of times — like countless two-bed units in series. This "polishes" water to very high purity (conductivity < ~ 0.1 µS/cm, silica < ~ 10–20 µg/L) for high-pressure boilers and electronics. For regeneration the resins are separated by backwashing (lighter anion on top), regenerated separately, then re-mixed with air (the animation shows the separation and remixing).

foundation: Vessels on level foundation or legs anchored; space above for resin loading and below for underdrain access.
alignment: Vessels plumb so the bed and distributors are level (uneven beds channel).
piping: Valve nest with service, backwash, regenerant, rinse; sample points before/after; acid/caustic-resistant lines and safety showers.
commissioning: Load support layers and resin (soaked), backwash to classify; first regeneration; rinse to quality; check conductivity/silica/hardness.

lubrication: No routine lubrication on static parts; lubricate valve stems and actuators per maker.

video_tutorials.title: Mixed Bed Polisher — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Mixed Bed Polisher.
A mixed-bed polisher contains cation and anion resins mixed intimately in one vessel.
The water meets H⁺ and OH⁻ sites alternately thousands of times, like many two-bed units in series, giving very pure water.
To regenerate, the resins are separated by backwashing, regenerated separately with acid and caustic, and re-mixed with air.
Typical applications include polishing after RO or two-bed DM for high-pressure boilers; electronics, pharmaceutical and laboratory water.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Mixed Bed Polisher works.
Pre-treated water enters at the top.
Mixed resins remove the remaining ions.
For regeneration, backwash separates the resins.
Acid and caustic regenerate each layer; air re-mixes.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
In service the cation and anion beads are mixed, so the water meets alternate H⁺ and OH⁻ exchange sites thousands of times — like countless two-bed units in series.

video_tutorials.title: Mixed Bed Polisher — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Mixed Bed Polisher.
Check outlet conductivity and silica.
Resin analysis.
Inspect interface collector and laterals.
Watch for poor separation: short runs, poor quality. Common cause: resin cross-contamination.
Watch for resin loss: resin downstream. Common cause: broken nozzle.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
